result.markdown: # Complex vector subsetting ![](/images/gear_1.png){style="width:200px; background:white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"} In this page we'll carry out some more complex subsetting. This will include: - Carrying out inverted subsetting with the minus symbol (`-`) - Subsetting when using `rep()` for our index - Using logical comparisons to subset - Even/odd extraction with modulus (`%%`) ## Inverted subsetting ![](/images/invert.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"} We have subsetted __vectors__ by specifying which indexes we want. We can also specify which indexes we don't want with `-`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} even_seq[-2] odd_seq[-3:-5] long_seq[c(-1,-2,-6)] ``` ::: ## Subsetting with rep() ![](/images/rep.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"} The `rep()` __function__ will replicate a __scalar/vector__ a specified amount of times. We will use this __function__ to overwrite our previously created __variables__ with longer versions. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #Replicate vector even_seq 2 times rep(x = even_seq, 2) #Replicate vector even_seq 4 times and then assign even_seq as the newly created vector even_seq <- rep(x = even_seq, 4) #More examples odd_seq <- rep(x = odd_seq, 4) long_seq <- rep(x = long_seq, 3) ``` ::: ## Logical subsetting ![](/images/true_false_bulb.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"} __Logical__ __operators__ can be used as indexes to subset __vectors__. Having a logical expression (i.e. 1 > 2) as the index will cause all TRUE positions to be included and all FALSE positions to be excluded. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} even_seq > 3 even_seq[even_seq > 2] odd_seq[odd_seq <= 1 ] long_seq <- long_seq[long_seq < 50] long_seq ``` ::: ::: {.callout-tip} If it is difficult to deduce what the above commands are doing you can run the part in the square brackets by itself. If you highlight code in the __script editor__ it will only run that part, excluding unhighlighted parts of script in the same line. ::: ## Modulus (%%) ![](/images/odd_or_even.png){style="width:300px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"} We will quickly look at a new __operator__, `%%`. This is the modulus __operator__, it divides two numbers and gives the remainder of the division. With the modulus __operator__, logical expressions, and subsetting we can extract even or odd numbers from a __vector__. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #First some basic modulus examples 2%%2 3%%2 #Create a vector with numbers 0 to 9 single_digit_vec <- 0:9 #Extract even numbers then odd numbers from the vector #We carry this out by determining if numbers are divisible by 2 or not even_seq <- single_digit_vec[(single_digit_vec %% 2) == 0 ] odd_seq <- single_digit_vec[(single_digit_vec %% 2) != 0] #We can determine which numbers in a vector are divisible by any specific number #Divisible by 3 #remember variable names cannot start with numbers divis_3_vec <- single_digit_vec[(single_digit_vec %% 3) == 0] #Divisible by 7 divis_7_vec <- single_digit_vec[(single_digit_vec %% 7) == 0] #Try out other numbers! ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: :::
